tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.

tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

3

7	|---|---|

12	
13	## 1. Overview
14	
15	The Resource Allocation & Help Desk Hub is one backend service of the Project Portal (PP). It manages a pool of physical lab equipment, software license keys and cloud credit vouchers, and handles requests for them from courses and research labs through a help desk ticket flow: request, sign-off, allocation, and for physical devices, return.
16	
17	The hub runs in its own containers, owns its own database and makes no calls to other Project Portal services. Data owned elsewhere (courses, labs, projects, users) comes from static mock data (section 7).
18	
19	Section 5 is the standardized specification for this service, copied unchanged. Section 6 clarifies the parts of it that are open to more than one reading.
20	
21	## 2. Tech stack and deployment
22	
23	- C# / ASP.NET Core Web API (.NET 10)
24	- PostgreSQL 18
25	- Entity Framework Core (Npgsql provider)
26	- Docker + Docker Compose
27	- JSON REST API under `/api/v1`
28	
29	The service runs with the existing `Dockerfile` and `docker-compose.yml`: an `api` container (ASP.NET Core, port 8080) and a `db` container (PostgreSQL 18). The existing `GET /api/v1/health` endpoint stays.
30	
31	## 3. Repository layout
32	
33	- Application code: `functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api/`
34	- Tests: `functional-codebase/tests/ResourceHub.Tests/`
35	- Build and run files (`ResourceHub.slnx`, `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml`, `global.json`, `Directory.Build.props`) stay at the repository root
36	
37	## 4. Roles
38	
39	| Role | What they do in this service |
40	|---|---|
41	| Course instructor | Submits resource request tickets for their course |
42	| Research lab faculty advisor | Submits resource request tickets for their research lab |
43	| IT director | Signs off on tickets (approves or rejects) |
44	| Administrator | Manages the asset catalog and runs the allocation that issues keys, vouchers and hardware |
45	
46	## 5. Standardized specification (verbatim)
47	
48	### Domain #2 The Resource Allocation & Help Desk Hub:
49	
50	This service handles the distribution of critical project assets, logging tracking parameters, software license keys, and cloud credit vouchers across active course groups and research labs.
51	
52	**Functional Requirements:**
53	
54	1. Asset Lifecycle & Inventory Allocation: Programmatically manage and monitor a pool of physical lab equipment (hardware units, laptops, IoT nodes), software license keys, and cloud credit vouchers. Each unique asset must be assigned a UUID, name, category, total stock, and availability metrics. Assets are allocated directly to an overarching academic course or research lab.
55	2. Polymorphic Balance and Status Tracking: Process transactional balance logic for heterogeneous assets. For cloud vouchers, it must manage strict numeric deduction checks (preventing balances from dropping below zero) and log high-value alphanumeric license tokens. For physical items, it must calculate active check-out duration tracking rules and maintain status flags (available, reserved, checkedout, overdue).
56	3. Help Desk Ticketing Pipeline: Process incoming resource requests from course instructor or research lab faculty advisor. The service must parse multi-tiered requests, track ticket lifecycles (pending, approved, rejected, allocated, closed), update project asset allocations dynamically upon IT director sign-off, and output comprehensive logging metrics.
57	4. Explicit Inventory Allocation Engine: The system must decouple administrative ticket review from physical inventory modification. Inventory values must only alter when a separate, dedicated allocation execution command is processed by an administrator, triggering atomic database deductions and issuing keys or hardware assignment tokens.
58	5. Complex Multi-Field Query: Support rich administrative and group queries. Users can search and filter the asset catalog and ticket logs simultaneously by status, asset category, requesting research lab or course.
59	
60	**REST APIs**
61	
62	| Endpoints | Verbs | Description |
63	|---|---|---|
64	| `/api/v1/assets` | POST, GET | Add an inventory asset item. Supplying multi-field search query parameters allows administrators and teams to filter active inventory listings by department program or availability state. |
65	| `/api/v1/assets/{asset_id}` | GET, PUT, DELETE | Read, update, and delete an inventory asset item. |
66	| `/api/v1/assets/{asset_id}/return` | POST | Processes the return of a checked-out physical device, increments the pool's remaining capacity stock, and records the return timestamp. |
67	| `/api/v1/assets/allocations` | GET | Read all active resource allocations, checked-out inventory metrics, and assigned software keys for a specific requesting research lab or course. |
68	| `/api/v1/assets/tickets` | POST, GET | Submit a new help desk resource request ticket or read a listing of all active requests filtered dynamically by status (pending/approved/allocated) or course section or project. |
69	| `/api/v1/assets/tickets/{ticket_id}` | PUT, DELETE, GET | Update a ticket's contents, delete a pending request, or fetch specific ticket metrics. A PUT request targeting this route handles the operational approval state transition. |
70	| `/api/v1/assets/tickets/{ticket_id}/allocate` | POST | Executes the real physical database mutation. This endpoint processes an approved ticket, atomically subtracts items from the main asset pool inventory, and establishes the active user allocation record. |
71	
72	## 6. Clarifications
73	
74	Where section 5 is open to more than one reading, build to these.
75	
76	1. **Kinds of asset:** each asset has a **type** (`physical`, `license`, `voucher`), which decides how its balance and status work, and a **category** (for example laptop, IoT node, IDE license, cloud credits), which is a descriptive label used for searching.
77	2. **Asset data:** UUID, name, type, category, home department program, total stock and availability. By type: a physical asset has a number of units and a default loan period in days; a license asset holds its license keys; a voucher asset holds a credit balance.
78	3. **Availability:** physical: number of units available, plus counts by status flag. License: keys not yet issued. Voucher: remaining balance. The availability filter on `GET /api/v1/assets` uses the status flags in requirement 2; license and voucher assets count as available while some stock or balance remains.
79	4. **When stock changes:** total stock is set when an asset is added or updated. Remaining stock and balances change only when a ticket is allocated (`POST .../allocate`) or a physical device is returned (`POST .../return`). The below-zero check in requirement 2 is made at allocation.
80	5. **License keys:** keys are stored with their asset, and each issued key is recorded with the ticket it was issued for and the time it was issued.
81	6. **Check-out duration:** a physical device's due date is its allocation date plus the loan period. A ticket may give a loan period for each physical asset it requests; otherwise the asset's default applies. A device is overdue once its due date has passed and it has not been returned.
82	7. **Ticket content:** a requester (a course instructor or a research lab faculty advisor), the course or the research lab the request is for, an optional project id, and one or more requested assets, each with a quantity (physical and license assets) or an amount (voucher assets). "Multi-tiered" means one ticket can request several assets.
83	8. **Ticket changes:** a ticket's contents can be updated, and the ticket deleted, only while it is `pending`. A PUT on `/api/v1/assets/tickets/{ticket_id}` also changes its state: `pending` to `approved` or `rejected` (IT director sign-off), and `allocated` to `closed`. Only `POST .../allocate` moves a ticket from `approved` to `allocated`.
84	9. **Not enough stock:** allocation is all or nothing. If any requested asset does not have enough stock or balance, nothing is allocated and the ticket stays `approved`, so allocation can be run again later.
85	10. **What allocation issues:** license: keys from the asset's pool. Voucher: the requested amount, deducted from the balance. Physical: one hardware assignment token for each device handed out, with its due date.
86	11. **Return:** one device per call, identified by its hardware assignment token. The return adds one to the asset's remaining stock and records the return time.
87	12. **Active allocations:** physical devices not yet returned, and license and voucher allocations whose ticket is not `closed`.
88	13. **Logging metrics:** an event is recorded for every ticket state change and every allocation attempt, including attempts that fail for lack of stock. `GET /api/v1/assets/tickets/{ticket_id}` returns the ticket with its events and timings (for example time from submission to approval and from approval to allocation).
89	14. **Filters:** query parameters can be combined. Assets: category, department program, availability. Tickets: status, asset category, course, research lab, project. Listings are paged and sorted newest first by creation date by default.
90	15. **Mock data:** courses (each including its section), research labs, projects, users and a few starting assets are seeded as static mock data with fixed ids, listed below, so tests and manual calls can use them. Each user has one of the four roles named in section 4: course instructor, research lab faculty advisor, IT director, administrator. No other service is called.

2. **Asset data:** UUID, name, type, category, home department program, total stock and availability. By type: a physical asset has a number of units and a default loan period in days; a license asset holds its license keys; a voucher asset holds a credit balance.

The availability filter on `GET /api/v1/assets` uses the status flags in requirement 2; license and voucher assets count as available while some stock or balance remains.
4. **When stock changes:** total stock is set when an asset is added or updated. Remaining stock and balances change only when a ticket is allocated (`POST .../allocate`) or a physical device is returned (`POST .../return`). The below-zero check in requirement 2 is made at allocation.
5. **License keys:** keys are stored with their asset, and each issued key is recorded with the ticket it was issued for and the time it was issued.
6. **Check-out duration:** a physical device's due date is its allocation date plus the loan period. A ticket may give a loan period for each physical asset it requests; otherwise the asset's default applies. A device is overdue once its due date has passed and it has not been returned.
7. **Ticket content:** a requester (a course instructor or a research lab faculty advisor), the course or the research lab the request is for, an optional project id, and one or more requested assets, each with a quantity (physical and license assets) or an amount (voucher assets). "Multi-tiered" means one ticket can request several assets.
8. **Ticket changes:** a ticket's contents can be updated, and the ticket deleted, only while it is `pending`. A PUT on `/api/v1/assets/tickets/{ticket_id}` also changes its state: `pending` to `approved` or `rejected` (IT director sign-off), and `allocated` to `closed`. Only `POST .../allocate` moves a ticket from `approved` to `allocated`.
9. **Not enough stock:** allocation is all or nothing. If any requested asset does not have enough stock or balance, nothing is allocated and the ticket stays `approved`, so allocation can be run again later.
10. **What allocation issues:** license: keys from the asset's pool. Voucher: the requested amount, deducted from the balance. Physical: one hardware assignment token for each device handed out, with its due date.
11. **Return:** one device per call, identified by its hardware assignment token. The return adds one to the asset's remaining stock and records the return time.
12. **Active allocations:** physical devices not yet returned, and license and voucher allocations whose ticket is not `closed`.
13. **Logging metrics:** an event is recorded for every ticket state change and every allocation attempt, including attempts that fail for lack of stock. `GET /api/v1/assets/tickets/{ticket_id}` returns the ticket with its events and timings (for example time from submission to approval and from approval to allocation).
14. **Filters:** query parameters can be combined. Assets: category, department program, availability. Tickets: status, asset category, course, research lab, project. Listings are paged and sorted newest first by creation date by default.
15. **Mock data:** courses (each including its section), research labs, projects, users and a few starting assets are seeded as static mock data with fixed ids, listed below, so tests and manual calls can use them. - `User`: id, name, role (`CourseInstructor`, `LabAdvisor`, `ItDirector`, `Administrator`), optional course id or lab id

**Assets**
- `Asset`: one table, with a `Type` column (physical, license or voucher) and some fields that only apply to one type.
  - **All types:** id, name, category, department program, created and updated times.
  - **Physical:** total units, available units, default loan days.
  - **Voucher:** total credit and balance, stored as `numeric(12,2)`.
  - **License:** total stock is the number of keys.
- Database check constraints stop available units from going below 0 or above the total, and stop the balance from going below 0. These back up the checks in code.
- A concurrency token (`xmin`) catches two updates that collide.
- `LicenseKey`: id, asset id, key value (unique), issued ticket id, issued time.
- `HardwareAssignment`: one row per device handed out. It holds the token, asset, ticket, check-out time, due time and return time.
- `VoucherAllocation`: ticket, asset, amount, allocated time.

**Tickets**
- `Ticket`: id, requester, course id or lab id (exactly one), optional project id, status, notes, and a timestamp for each stage: created, approved or rejected, allocated, closed. Also who signed off, and a concurrency token.
- `TicketItem`: asset id, plus a quantity (physical and license) or an amount (voucher), plus optional loan days for physical assets.
- `TicketEvent`: ticket, event type, actor, time, short detail. Event types are submitted, updated, approved, rejected, allocation succeeded, allocation failed (with the reason) and closed.

## Choices I'd make where the spec is open (all go in the notes)

1. **Acting user:** the caller says who they are with an `X-User-Id` header naming one of the mock users. Without it they get 401; with the wrong role they get 403. The rules: instructors and advisors submit tickets only for their own course or lab; the IT director approves or rejects; the administrator manages assets, allocates, returns and closes. This is a stand-in for real authentication, not authentication itself, and the notes will say so. Health stays open without the header, which the existing test already expects.
2. **Status flags:** `reserved` means units requested on approved tickets that haven't been allocated yet. `checkedout` means devices out and not past due; `overdue` means devices out and past due. The `availability` filter takes one of those flags. For license and voucher assets it only matches `available`.
3. **Changing total stock on PUT:**
   - Physical and voucher: the remaining stock moves by the same amount as the total. The change is refused (409) if the remaining stock would go below zero.
   - License: PUT can add keys or remove keys that haven't been issued. Issued keys can never be removed.
4. **Deleting an asset:** refused (409) if any ticket or allocation refers to it.
5. **Protecting license keys:** unissued keys are never returned by the API, only their count. Issued keys are returned only in the allocate response and the allocations listing. Key values are never written to logs.
6. **Atomic allocation:** everything runs in one transaction. The ticket row and the asset rows are locked with `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`, assets in id order so two allocations can't deadlock. Stock is checked for every item, and then everything is deducted, or nothing is. A failed attempt is recorded as an event; the transaction is rolled back and the event saved separately so it survives.
7. **`GET /assets/allocations`** requires `courseId` or `researchLabId`.
8. **Errors and paging:** errors come back as ProblemDetails with status 400, 401, 403, 404 or 409. Listings take `page` and `pageSize` (pageSize at most 100) and are sorted newest first.
9. **Route clash:** `/assets/{asset_id}` and `/assets/tickets` look alike. Adding a `:guid` route constraint keeps them apart.
10. **Creating the schema:** EF Core migrations, applied when the app starts. This adds `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Design`, which changes `packages.lock.json`. If `Directory.Build.props` locks package restore, I'll tell you before changing anything there.

## Files (all under `functional-codebase/`)

- `src/ResourceHub.Api/`
  - `Domain/`: entities and enums
  - `Data/HubDbContext.cs`: entity configuration and constraints
  - `Data/MockData.cs`: seed data
  - `Migrations/`
  - `Security/CurrentUser.cs`: reads the `X-User-Id` header and checks roles
  - `Contracts/`: request and response DTOs, with validation
  - `Services/`: `AssetService`, `TicketService`, `AllocationService`
  - `Controllers/`: `AssetsController`, `TicketsController` (includes allocate), `AllocationsController`
  - `Program.cs`: register the services, ProblemDetails and the startup migration
- `tests/ResourceHub.Tests/`
  - A database fixture that creates a throwaway PostgreSQL database per test class and drops it afterwards
  - `AssetEndpointTests`, `TicketEndpointTests`, `AllocationEndpointTests`, including the over-allocation case

## Build order

1. Domain, DbContext, seed data, first migration. Build.
2. Assets: CRUD and filters.
3. Tickets: CRUD, state changes, events and timings.
4. Allocate and return, then the allocations listing.
5. Integration tests. Run them against the database.
6. `docker compose up` and a walkthrough with the mock data, including the over-allocation attempt.
7. README update and the task note in `MyAI/PA2`.

**Files outside `functional-codebase/`:** I expect not to change any. I'll read `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml` and `Directory.Build.props` (asking you for each) when I get to build and run. If one needs to change, for example a connection-string environment variable, I'll tell you what and why first.

One small thing I noticed: [HealthController.cs:4](src/ResourceHub.Api/Controllers/HealthController.cs:4) has a header copied from the DbContext ("Generated the DbContext"). I'll leave it unless you want it fixed.

services:
  db:
    image: postgres:18
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: resourcehub
      POSTGRES_USER: resourcehub
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-resourcehub_dev}
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      # postgres:18 keeps data under /var/lib/postgresql/<version>, so mount the parent.
      - db-data:/var/lib/postgresql
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U resourcehub -d resourcehub"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10

  api:
    build: .
    environment:
      ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: Production
      ConnectionStrings__HubDb: "Host=db;Port=5432;Database=resourcehub;Username=resourcehub;Password=${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-resourcehub_dev};Timeout=5"
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy

volumes:
  db-data:

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
# AI Contribution Weight: [100%] AI Generated / [0%] Human Refactored

# ---- build stage: .NET SDK ----
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 AS build
WORKDIR /src

# Restore first so the package layer is cached between code changes.
COPY global.json Directory.Build.props ./
COPY functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api/ResourceHub.Api.csproj functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api/packages.lock.json src/ResourceHub.Api/
RUN dotnet restore src/ResourceHub.Api/ResourceHub.Api.csproj --locked-mode

COPY functional-codebase/src/ src/
RUN dotnet publish src/ResourceHub.Api/ResourceHub.Api.csproj \
    --configuration Release --no-restore --output /app/publish /p:UseAppHost=false

# ---- runtime stage: ASP.NET Core runtime ----
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0 AS runtime
WORKDIR /app

ENV ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS=8080
EXPOSE 8080

COPY --from=build /app/publish .

# Built-in non-root user in the .NET images.
USER $APP_UID

ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "ResourceHub.Api.dll"]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Walks one full ticket flow against the docker compose stack using the seeded mock data.
set -u
B=http://localhost:8080/api/v1
CHEN=40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001
FERREIRA=40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003
BLAKE=40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005
RIVERA=40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000006
CS501=10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001
DSLAB=20000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001
DASH=30000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001
LAPTOP=50000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002
JB=50000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003
CLOUD=50000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004

call() { # user method url [body]
  local user=$1 method=$2 url=$3 body=${4:-}
  local args=(-s -o /tmp/wt_body -w '%{http_code}' -X "$method" "$B$url" -H 'Content-Type: application/json')
  [ -n "$user" ] && args+=(-H "X-User-Id: $user")
  [ -n "$body" ] && args+=(-d "$body")
  local code; code=$(curl "${args[@]}")
  echo "### $method $url  ->  HTTP $code"
}
show() { jq -c "$1" /tmp/wt_body; echo; }

call "" GET /health; show .
call $CHEN GET "/assets?pageSize=10"; show '.items[] | {name,type,remainingStock}'

call $CHEN POST /assets/tickets "{\"courseId\":\"$CS501\",\"projectId\":\"$DASH\",\"notes\":\"Sprint 3\",\"items\":[{\"assetId\":\"$LAPTOP\",\"quantity\":2,\"loanDays\":21},{\"assetId\":\"$JB\",\"quantity\":1},{\"assetId\":\"$CLOUD\",\"amount\":750}]}"
T=$(jq -r .id /tmp/wt_body); show '{id,status,items:[.items[]|{assetName,quantity,amount,loanDays}]}'

call $BLAKE GET "/assets/tickets?status=pending&courseId=$CS501"; show '{totalCount, ids:[.items[].id]}'
call $BLAKE PUT /assets/tickets/$T '{"status":"approved","comment":"Within budget"}'; show '{status,signedOffAt,timings}'
call $RIVERA POST /assets/tickets/$T/allocate; show .
TOKEN=$(jq -r '.devices[0].token' /tmp/wt_body)

call $CHEN GET "/assets/allocations?courseId=$CS501"; show '{metrics, devices:[.devices[]|{token,assetName,dueAt,status}], licenseKeys:[.licenseKeys[]|{assetName,key}], vouchers:[.vouchers[]|{assetName,amount}]}'
call $RIVERA POST /assets/$LAPTOP/return "{\"token\":\"$TOKEN\"}"; show .
call $RIVERA GET /assets/$LAPTOP; show '{name,totalStock,remainingStock,physical}'
call $RIVERA PUT /assets/tickets/$T '{"status":"closed","comment":"Sprint finished"}'; show '{status,closedAt}'
call $CHEN GET /assets/tickets/$T; show '{status, events:[.events[]|{type,detail}], timings}'

echo "===== Over-allocation: 4 JetBrains keys requested, pool has 3 (2 left) ====="
call $FERREIRA POST /assets/tickets "{\"researchLabId\":\"$DSLAB\",\"items\":[{\"assetId\":\"$JB\",\"quantity\":4},{\"assetId\":\"$CLOUD\",\"amount\":100}]}"
T2=$(jq -r .id /tmp/wt_body); show '{id,status}'
call $BLAKE PUT /assets/tickets/$T2 '{"status":"approved"}'; show '{status}'
call $RIVERA POST /assets/tickets/$T2/allocate; show .
call $RIVERA GET /assets/$JB; show '{remainingStock,license}'
call $RIVERA GET /assets/$CLOUD; show '{remainingStock,voucher}'
call $FERREIRA GET /assets/tickets/$T2; show '{status, events:[.events[]|{type,detail}], timings}'

echo "===== Auth checks ====="
call "" GET /assets; show '{status,title}'
call $CHEN POST /assets/tickets/$T2/allocate; show '{status,title}'

1	# Resource Allocation & Help Desk Hub
2	
3	ASP.NET Core Web API (.NET 10) + PostgreSQL 18. See [spec-domain2.md](spec-domain2.md) for the full design.
4	
5	**Current state: barebones.** Only `GET /api/v1/health` exists. It checks the PostgreSQL
6	connection through an EF Core `DbContext` (no tables yet).
7	
8	## Layout
9	
10	```
11	global.json                  # pins .NET SDK 10
12	Directory.Build.props        # turns on NuGet lock files (packages.lock.json)
13	.github/workflows/devsecops.yml  # CI: build, test, image, Trivy, Semgrep, SonarQube Cloud
14	Dockerfile                   # multi-stage: SDK build -> ASP.NET runtime
15	docker-compose.yml           # api (:8080) + db (PostgreSQL 18, :5432)
16	ResourceHub.slnx
17	functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api/         # Web API (Controllers/, Data/, Program.cs)
18	functional-codebase/tests/ResourceHub.Tests/     # xUnit integration tests (WebApplicationFactory)
19	```
20	
21	## Prerequisites
22	
23	- .NET SDK 10 (for local build/test)
24	- Docker with Compose v2
25	
26	## Run with Docker Compose
27	
28	```bash
29	docker compose up --build -d
30	```
31	
32	```bash
33	curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/health
34	```
35	
36	Expected when the database is up:
37	
38	```
39	HTTP/1.1 200 OK
40	{"status":"ok","database":"ok"}
41	```
42	
43	Stop the database to see the unhealthy response:
44	
45	```bash
46	docker compose stop db
47	```
48	
49	```bash
50	curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/health
51	```
52	
53	```
54	HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
55	{"status":"unhealthy","database":"unreachable"}
56	```
57	
58	Start it again with `docker compose start db`. Shut everything down with:
59	
60	```bash
61	docker compose down
62	```
63	
64	Add `-v` to also delete the database volume.
65	
66	The database password defaults to `resourcehub_dev`, a local development value. Override it by
67	setting `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` in your shell or in a `.env` file next to `docker-compose.yml`
68	(`.env` is git-ignored). Changing it after the volume exists needs `docker compose down -v`.
69	
70	## Build and run locally (without the api container)
71	
72	```bash
73	docker compose up -d db
74	```
75	
76	```bash
77	dotnet run --project functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api
78	```
79	
80	Local runs use the `Development` environment, which reads the connection string from
81	`functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api/appsettings.Development.json` (`localhost:5432`). The URL is printed on
82	start-up (default `http://localhost:5184/api/v1/health`).
83	
84	## Test
85	
86	```bash
87	dotnet test
88	```
89	
90	Without a database, the PostgreSQL-dependent test is skipped and the rest run against an
91	unreachable connection string (checks the `503` path). To also run the `200` test, start the db
92	container and point the tests at it:
93	
94	```bash
95	docker compose up -d db
96	```
97	
98	```bash
99	RESOURCEHUB_TEST_DB="Host=localhost;Port=5432;Database=resourcehub;Username=resourcehub;Password=resourcehub_dev" dotnet test
100	```
101	
102	## Configuration
103	
104	| Setting | Where | Notes |
105	|---|---|---|
106	| `ConnectionStrings:HubDb` | env `ConnectionStrings__HubDb` (compose) or `appsettings.Development.json` | Required; app fails on first DB use without it |
107	| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | shell / `.env` | Used by both containers; default `resourcehub_dev` |
108	| `ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS` | Dockerfile | `8080` |
109	
110	## NuGet lock files
111	
112	Each project has a `packages.lock.json` that pins every direct and transitive package. CI and the
113	Dockerfile restore with `--locked-mode`, so a restore that would change the lock file fails. After
114	adding or upgrading a package, run `dotnet restore` and commit the updated lock files. Trivy also
115	reads these files to find NuGet dependencies; without them it detects none.
116	
117	## CI (GitHub Actions)
118	
119	`.github/workflows/devsecops.yml` runs on every push to `main` and on pull requests.
120	
121	| Job | Steps |
122	|---|---|
123	| Build, test, image, Trivy, SonarQube | Restore, SonarQube begin, build (Release), test (with a PostgreSQL 18 service container, coverage), SonarQube end, `docker build`, Trivy dependency scan, Trivy image scan |
124	| Semgrep | Open-source Semgrep CLI with the public `p/csharp` rules (no account or token) |
125

# Resource Allocation & Help Desk Hub

ASP.NET Core Web API (.NET 10) + PostgreSQL 18. See [spec-domain2.md](spec-domain2.md) for the full design.

**Current state: barebones.** Only `GET /api/v1/health` exists. It checks the PostgreSQL
connection through an EF Core `DbContext` (no tables yet).

## Layout

```
global.json                  # pins .NET SDK 10
Directory.Build.props        # turns on NuGet lock files (packages.lock.json)
.github/workflows/devsecops.yml  # CI: build, test, image, Trivy, Semgrep, SonarQube Cloud
Dockerfile                   # multi-stage: SDK build -> ASP.NET runtime
docker-compose.yml           # api (:8080) + db (PostgreSQL 18, :5432)
ResourceHub.slnx
functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api/         # Web API (Controllers/, Data/, Program.cs)
functional-codebase/tests/ResourceHub.Tests/     # xUnit integration tests (WebApplicationFactory)
```

## Prerequisites

- .NET SDK 10 (for local build/test)
- Docker with Compose v2

## Run with Docker Compose

```bash
docker compose up --build -d
```

```bash
curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/health
```

Expected when the database is up:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"status":"ok","database":"ok"}
```

Stop the database to see the unhealthy response:

```bash
docker compose stop db
```

```bash
curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/health
```

```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
{"status":"unhealthy","database":"unreachable"}
```

Start it again with `docker compose start db`. Shut everything down with:

```bash
docker compose down
```

Add `-v` to also delete the database volume.

The database password defaults to `resourcehub_dev`, a local development value. Override it by
setting `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` in your shell or in a `.env` file next to `docker-compose.yml`
(`.env` is git-ignored). Changing it after the volume exists needs `docker compose down -v`.

## Build and run locally (without the api container)

```bash
docker compose up -d db
```

```bash
dotnet run --project functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api
```

Local runs use the `Development` environment, which reads the connection string from
`functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api/appsettings.Development.json` (`localhost:5432`). The URL is printed on
start-up (default `http://localhost:5184/api/v1/health`).

## Test

```bash
dotnet test
```

Without a database, the PostgreSQL-dependent test is skipped and the rest run against an
unreachable connection string (checks the `503` path). To also run the `200` test, start the db
container and point the tests at it:

```bash
docker compose up -d db
```

```bash
RESOURCEHUB_TEST_DB="Host=localhost;Port=5432;Database=resourcehub;Username=resourcehub;Password=resourcehub_dev" dotnet test
```

## Configuration

| Setting | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ConnectionStrings:HubDb` | env `ConnectionStrings__HubDb` (compose) or `appsettings.Development.json` | Required; app fails on first DB use without it |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | shell / `.env` | Used by both containers; default `resourcehub_dev` |
| `ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS` | Dockerfile | `8080` |

## NuGet lock files

Each project has a `packages.lock.json` that pins every direct and transitive package. CI and the
Dockerfile restore with `--locked-mode`, so a restore that would change the lock file fails. After
adding or upgrading a package, run `dotnet restore` and commit the updated lock files. Trivy also
reads these files to find NuGet dependencies; without them it detects none.

## CI (GitHub Actions)

`.github/workflows/devsecops.yml` runs on every push to `main` and on pull requests.

| Job | Steps |
|---|---|
| Build, test, image, Trivy, SonarQube | Restore, SonarQube begin, build (Release), test (with a PostgreSQL 18 service container, coverage), SonarQube end, `docker build`, Trivy dependency scan, Trivy image scan |
| Semgrep | Open-source Semgrep CLI with the public `p/csharp` rules (no account or token) |

Only a broken build, a failing test or a failing Docker build fails the run. Scanner findings
are reported in the logs and uploaded as artifacts (`trivy-reports`, `semgrep-reports`,
`sonarqube-report`, `test-results`) without failing the run. SonarQube Cloud results are on
the SonarQube Cloud dashboard; it needs the `SONAR_TOKEN` repository secret and is skipped
when the secret is not available (for example, pull requests from forks).

input.new_string:
ASP.NET Core Web API (.NET 10) + PostgreSQL 18 + EF Core. See [spec-domain2.md](spec-domain2.md) for the full design.

The hub manages a pool of physical lab equipment, software license keys and cloud credit
vouchers, and the help desk tickets that request them: submit, IT director sign-off,
administrator allocation, device return, close. All endpoints in spec section 5 are
implemented, plus the existing `GET /api/v1/health`.

## Layout

```
global.json                  # pins .NET SDK 10
Directory.Build.props        # turns on NuGet lock files (packages.lock.json)
.github/workflows/devsecops.yml  # CI: build, test, image, Trivy, Semgrep, SonarQube Cloud
Dockerfile                   # multi-stage: SDK build -> ASP.NET runtime
docker-compose.yml           # api (:8080) + db (PostgreSQL 18, :5432)
ResourceHub.slnx
functional-codebase/dotnet-tools.json            # local dotnet-ef tool (migrations)
functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api/
  Controllers/   # health, assets, tickets (+ allocate), allocations
  Services/      # AssetService, TicketService, AllocationService
  Domain/        # entities and enums
  Contracts/     # request/response DTOs and validation
  Data/          # HubDbContext, MockData (seed), DatabaseMigrator, Migrations/
  Security/      # X-User-Id authentication handler and roles
functional-codebase/tests/ResourceHub.Tests/     # xUnit integration tests (WebApplicationFactory)
```

## Calling the API

Every endpoint except `/api/v1/health` needs an `X-User-Id` header naming one of the seeded
mock users. A missing or unknown id gets `401`; the wrong role gets `403`. **This header is a
stand-in for real authentication, not authentication itself:** the service trusts whoever
sends it. Replace it with a signed token before any real deployment.

| User | Id | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Dr. Maya Chen | `40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001` | Course instructor (CS501 A1) |
| Prof. Daniel Okafor | `40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002` | Course instructor (EE580 B1) |
| Dr. Lucas Ferreira | `40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003` | Lab advisor (Data Science Lab) |
| Dr. Priya Raman | `40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004` | Lab advisor (Embedded Systems Lab) |
| Jordan Blake | `40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005` | IT director |
| Sam Rivera | `40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000006` | Administrator |

Courses, labs, projects and the four starting assets are seeded with the ids in spec section 7.

| Endpoint | Who | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/assets` | administrator | `type` is `physical` (`totalUnits`, `defaultLoanDays`), `license` (`licenseKeys`) or `voucher` (`totalCredit`) |
| `GET /api/v1/assets` | any user | Filters: `category`, `departmentProgram`, `type`, `availability` (`available`, `reserved`, `checkedout`, `overdue`), `page`, `pageSize` |
| `GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/assets/{id}` | read: any user; change: administrator | License keys are shown masked (`****Q9XA`); PUT can add keys or remove unissued ones |
| `POST /api/v1/assets/{id}/return` | administrator | Body `{"token":"HW-..."}`: returns one device |
| `GET /api/v1/assets/allocations` | own course/lab, or staff | Needs `courseId` or `researchLabId` |
| `POST /api/v1/assets/tickets` | course instructor, lab advisor | For your own course or lab; items have `quantity` (physical, license) or `amount` (voucher) |
| `GET /api/v1/assets/tickets` | own course/lab, or staff | Filters: `status`, `assetCategory`, `courseId`, `researchLabId`, `projectId`, `page`, `pageSize` |
| `GET /api/v1/assets/tickets/{id}` | own course/lab, or staff | Includes events and timings |
| `PUT /api/v1/assets/tickets/{id}` | requester (contents, while pending); IT director (`approved`/`rejected`); administrator (`closed`) | Send either `{"status":...,"comment":...}` or new contents, not both |
| `DELETE /api/v1/assets/tickets/{id}` | requester or administrator | Pending tickets only |
| `POST /api/v1/assets/tickets/{id}/allocate` | administrator | All or nothing. `409` with a `shortages` list if stock is short; the ticket stays approved |

Errors are returned as ProblemDetails (`application/problem+json`). Enum values are snake_case
strings (`course_instructor`, `allocation_failed`).

Example: Dr. Chen requests two laptops and one IDE license for CS501:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/assets/tickets \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-User-Id: 40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001' \
  -d '{"courseId":"10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","items":[{"assetId":"50000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002","quantity":2},{"assetId":"50000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003","quantity":1}]}'
```

**Current state: barebones.** Only `GET /api/v1/health` exists. It checks the PostgreSQL
connection through an EF Core `DbContext` (no tables yet).

## Layout

```
global.json                  # pins .NET SDK 10
Directory.Build.props        # turns on NuGet lock files (packages.lock.json)
.github/workflows/devsecops.yml  # CI: build, test, image, Trivy, Semgrep, SonarQube Cloud
Dockerfile                   # multi-stage: SDK build -> ASP.NET runtime
docker-compose.yml           # api (:8080) + db (PostgreSQL 18, :5432)
ResourceHub.slnx
functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api/         # Web API (Controllers/, Data/, Program.cs)
functional-codebase/tests/ResourceHub.Tests/     # xUnit integration tests (WebApplicationFactory)
```

## Prerequisites

- .NET SDK 10 (for local build/test)
- Docker with Compose v2

## Run with Docker Compose

```bash
docker compose up --build -d
```

```bash
curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/health
```

Expected when the database is up:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"status":"ok","database":"ok"}
```

Stop the database to see the unhealthy response:

```bash
docker compose stop db
```

```bash
curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/health
```

```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
{"status":"unhealthy","database":"unreachable"}
```

Start it again with `docker compose start db`. Shut everything down with:

```bash
docker compose down
```

Add `-v` to also delete the database volume.

The database password defaults to `resourcehub_dev`, a local development value. Override it by
setting `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` in your shell or in a `.env` file next to `docker-compose.yml`
(`.env` is git-ignored). Changing it after the volume exists needs `docker compose down -v`.

## Build and run locally (without the api container)

```bash
docker compose up -d db
```

```bash
dotnet run --project functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api
```

Local runs use the `Development` environment, which reads the connection string from
`functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api/appsettings.Development.json` (`localhost:5432`). The URL is printed on
start-up (default `http://localhost:5184/api/v1/health`).

## Test

```bash
dotnet test
```

Without a database, the PostgreSQL-dependent test is skipped and the rest run against an
unreachable connection string (checks the `503` path). To also run the `200` test, start the db
container and point the tests at it:

```bash
docker compose up -d db
```

```bash
RESOURCEHUB_TEST_DB="Host=localhost;Port=5432;Database=resourcehub;Username=resourcehub;Password=resourcehub_dev" dotnet test
```

## Configuration

| Setting | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ConnectionStrings:HubDb` | env `ConnectionStrings__HubDb` (compose) or `appsettings.Development.json` | Required; app fails on first DB use without it |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | shell / `.env` | Used by both containers; default `resourcehub_dev` |
| `ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS` | Dockerfile | `8080` |

## NuGet lock files

Each project has a `packages.lock.json` that pins every direct and transitive package. CI and the
Dockerfile restore with `--locked-mode`, so a restore that would change the lock file fails. After
adding or upgrading a package, run `dotnet restore` and commit the updated lock files. Trivy also
reads these files to find NuGet dependencies; without them it detects none.

## CI (GitHub Actions)

`.github/workflows/devsecops.yml` runs on every push to `main` and on pull requests.

| Job | Steps |
|---|---|
| Build, test, image, Trivy, SonarQube | Restore, SonarQube begin, build (Release), test (with a PostgreSQL 18 service container, coverage), SonarQube end, `docker build`, Trivy dependency scan, Trivy image scan |
| Semgrep | Open-source Semgrep CLI with the public `p/csharp` rules (no account or token) |

Only a broken build, a failing test or a failing Docker build fails the run. Scanner findings
are reported in the logs and uploaded as artifacts (`trivy-reports`, `semgrep-reports`,
`sonarqube-report`, `test-results`) without failing the run. SonarQube Cloud results are on
the SonarQube Cloud dashboard; it needs the `SONAR_TOKEN` repository secret and is skipped
when the secret is not available (for example, pull requests from forks).

| Dr. Priya Raman | `40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004` | Lab advisor (Embedded Systems Lab) |

| `GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/assets/{id}` | read: any user; change: administrator | License keys are shown masked (`****Q9XA`); PUT can add keys or remove unissued ones |
| `POST /api/v1/assets/{id}/return` | administrator | Body `{"token":"HW-..."}`: returns one device |
| `GET /api/v1/assets/allocations` | own course/lab, or staff | Needs `courseId` or `researchLabId` |

| `GET /api/v1/assets/tickets/{id}` | own course/lab, or staff | Includes events and timings |

  -H 'X-User-Id: 40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001' \
  -d '{"courseId":"10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","items":[{"assetId":"50000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002","quantity":2},{"assetId":"50000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003","quantity":1}]}'
```

- .NET SDK 10 (for local build/test)
- Docker with Compose v2

## Run with Docker Compose

```bash
docker compose up --build -d
```

On start-up the API applies the EF Core migrations, which create the schema and seed the mock
data. If the database is not reachable yet it retries every 5 seconds; health answers `503`
meanwhile.

```bash
curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/health
```

Expected when the database is up:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"status":"ok","database":"ok"}
```

Stop the database to see the unhealthy response:

```bash
docker compose stop db
```

```bash
curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/health
```

```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
{"status":"unhealthy","database":"unreachable"}
```

Start it again with `docker compose start db`. Shut everything down with:

```bash
docker compose down
```

Add `-v` to also delete the database volume.

The database password defaults to `resourcehub_dev`, a local development value. Override it by
setting `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` in your shell or in a `.env` file next to `docker-compose.yml`
(`.env` is git-ignored). Changing it after the volume exists needs `docker compose down -v`.

## Build and run locally (without the api container)

```bash
docker compose up -d db
```

```bash
dotnet run --project functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api
```

Local runs use the `Development` environment, which reads the connection string from
`functional-codebase/src/ResourceHub.Api/appsettings.Development.json` (`localhost:5432`). The URL is printed on
start-up (default `http://localhost:5184/api/v1/health`).

## Test

```bash
dotnet test
```

Without a database, the PostgreSQL-dependent test is skipped and the rest run against an
unreachable connection string (checks the `503` path). To also run the `200` test, start the db
container and point the tests at it:

```bash
docker compose up -d db
```

```bash
RESOURCEHUB_TEST_DB="Host=localhost;Port=5432;Database=resourcehub;Username=resourcehub;Password=resourcehub_dev" dotnet test
```

## Configuration

| Setting | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ConnectionStrings:HubDb` | env `ConnectionStrings__HubDb` (compose) or `appsettings.Development.json` | Required; app fails on first DB use without it |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | shell / `.env` | Used by both containers; default `resourcehub_dev` |
| `ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS` | Dockerfile | `8080` |

## NuGet lock files

Each project has a `packages.lock.json` that pins every direct and transitive package. CI and the
Dockerfile restore with `--locked-mode`, so a restore that would change the lock file fails. After
adding or upgrading a package, run `dotnet restore` and commit the updated lock files. Trivy also
reads these files to find NuGet dependencies; without them it detects none.

`.github/workflows/devsecops.yml` runs on every push to `main` and on pull requests.

| Job | Steps |
|---|---|
| Build, test, image, Trivy, SonarQube | Restore, SonarQube begin, build (Release), test (with a PostgreSQL 18 service container, coverage), SonarQube end, `docker build`, Trivy dependency scan, Trivy image scan |
| Semgrep | Open-source Semgrep CLI with the public `p/csharp` rules (no account or token) |

Only a broken build, a failing test or a failing Docker build fails the run. Scanner findings
are reported in the logs and uploaded as artifacts (`trivy-reports`, `semgrep-reports`,
`sonarqube-report`, `test-results`) without failing the run. SonarQube Cloud results are on
the SonarQube Cloud dashboard; it needs the `SONAR_TOKEN` repository secret and is skipped
when the secret is not available (for example, pull requests from forks).

# 2026-11-14 · 01 · Resource Hub build (PA2)

## What I was asked

Build the Resource Allocation & Help Desk Hub from `spec-domain2.md` on top of the existing
`functional-codebase/` app: every endpoint in section 5, following the clarifications in section 6,
with the section 7 mock data seeded under its fixed ids. Keep `GET /api/v1/health` as it is. Add
integration tests for the main path of every endpoint, run them against the database, walk a full
flow through `docker compose up`, try to allocate more license keys than exist, update the
README. Plan first and wait for a go-ahead; no commits.

## What I did

- Gave a plan (data model, files, build order, open choices). It was approved as written.
- Built the data model, a migration (schema and seed), the X-User-Id stand-in authentication, the
  three services, four controllers, and startup changes.
- Wrote 23 new integration tests (3 health tests already existed).
- Ran the tests against PostgreSQL 18 (the compose `db` container), then ran the stack with
  docker compose and walked one full flow plus the over-allocation case.
- Updated `README.md`.

## Files created / changed

All paths under `cs763-resource-hub/`.

**Created**
- `functional-codebase/dotnet-tools.json`: local `dotnet-ef` 10.0.4 (the global one is 6.0.2, too old for EF 10)
- `src/ResourceHub.Api/Domain/`: `Enums.cs`, `ReferenceData.cs`, `Asset.cs`, `Ticket.cs`, `Allocations.cs`
- `src/ResourceHub.Api/Data/`: `MockData.cs`, `DatabaseMigrator.cs`, `Migrations/` (`InitialHub` plus the model snapshot)
- `src/ResourceHub.Api/Security/UserHeaderAuthentication.cs`
- `src/ResourceHub.Api/Contracts/`: `AssetContracts.cs`, `TicketContracts.cs`
- `src/ResourceHub.Api/Services/`: `ServiceResult.cs`, `AssetService.cs`, `TicketService.cs`, `AllocationService.cs`
- `src/ResourceHub.Api/Controllers/`: `HubControllerBase.cs`, `AssetsController.cs`, `TicketsController.cs`, `AllocationsController.cs`
- `tests/ResourceHub.Tests/`: `TestSupport.cs`, `AssetEndpointTests.cs`, `TicketEndpointTests.cs`, `AllocationEndpointTests.cs`

**Changed**
- `src/ResourceHub.Api/Program.cs`: services, auth, JSON enums, ProblemDetails, migrator
- `src/ResourceHub.Api/Data/HubDbContext.cs`: entities, constraints, seed
- `src/ResourceHub.Api/ResourceHub.Api.csproj` and `packages.lock.json`: added `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Design` 10.0.4 (PrivateAssets=all)
- `README.md`

**Not changed:** `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml`, `ResourceHub.slnx`, `global.json`,
`Directory.Build.props`. None needed changes.

## Decisions I made (and why)

Choices where the spec is open to more than one reading:

1. **Who the caller is:** an `X-User-Id` header names a mock user; a missing or unknown id gets
   401 and the wrong role gets 403. This is a stand-in, not authentication: anyone can claim any id.
   I chose it so role rules can be enforced and tested now. It needs replacing with real
   authentication (a signed token) before any real use.
2. **Who may do what:**
   - Instructors and advisors submit tickets only for their own course or lab.
   - The IT director approves or rejects.
   - The administrator manages assets, allocates, returns devices and closes tickets.
   - Delete: the requester or the administrator. Contents: the requester only.
3. **What requesters can see:** they see only their own course's or lab's tickets and allocations.
   The IT director and administrator see everything. Another group's ticket returns 404 rather
   than 403, so ticket ids can't be probed. A request for another group's allocations gets 403.
   The asset catalog is open to every known user.
4. **Status flags:**
   - `reserved`: units requested on approved tickets not yet allocated.
   - `checkedout`: out and not past due.
   - `overdue`: out and past due.
   - The `availability` filter takes one flag. License and voucher assets only match `available`
     (while keys or balance remain).
5. **Changing totals with PUT:**
   - Physical and voucher: remaining stock moves by the same amount as the total. The change is
     refused (409) if remaining would go below zero.
   - License: PUT adds keys (`addLicenseKeys`) or removes unissued ones (`removeLicenseKeyIds`).
     Issued keys can't be removed.
   - PUT replaces the asset's details (name, category, program and the type's stock fields).
     The type can't change.
6. **Protecting license keys:** key values never appear in the catalog, only masked (`****Q9XA`).
   They are returned only by allocate and by the allocations listing. They are never logged and
   never put in event details. A duplicate-key error doesn't say which key, so the API can't be
   used to probe for key values.
7. **Allocation:** one transaction.
   - The ticket row and the asset rows are locked with `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`, assets in id order
     so two allocations can't deadlock.
   - Every item is checked before anything is deducted.
   - When stock is short: rollback, a 409 with a `shortages` list, and an `allocation_failed`
     event saved after the rollback. The ticket stays approved.
   - Allocating a ticket that isn't approved also logs an `allocation_failed` event (it counts
     as an attempt).
   - Database check constraints stop units or balance going below 0 or above the total, as a backstop.
8. **Hardware tokens:** `HW-` plus 24 hex characters (96 random bits from `RandomNumberGenerator`).
9. **PUT on a ticket:** either `{status, comment}` or new contents (`items`, `projectId`, `notes`),
   never both (400). New contents replace the old ones. The course or lab can't change. A status
   of `allocated` is refused (409): use `/allocate`.
10. **Deleting a pending ticket** removes its items and events too (cascade). The deletion is
    recorded in the application log, not as an event.
11. **Ticket listing:** returns all statuses unless `status` is given. I didn't read "active
    requests" as hiding closed or rejected tickets by default.
12. **Asset delete:** refused (409) if any ticket item, allocation or issued key refers to the asset.
13. **Timings:** in seconds. Submission to sign-off, approval to allocation, allocation to close,
    plus the number of attempts and failed attempts.
14. **Enums in JSON** are snake_case strings, and numbers are refused. `checkedout` is spelled as
    in the spec.
15. **Paging:** `page` and `pageSize` (default 20, at most 100), newest first by `createdAt`.
16. **Migrations run at startup** in a background service that retries every 5 s. This keeps the
    existing health 503 test working: the app doesn't crash when the database is down. The tests
    turn it off and migrate their own throwaway database instead.
17. **Ids** for new rows use `Guid.NewGuid()` (UUID v4).

## Problems / things I couldn't do

- The global `dotnet-ef` (6.0.2) can't work with EF Core 10, so I added a local tool manifest.
  It ended up at `functional-codebase/dotnet-tools.json` rather than `.config/`, which is the newer SDK's default.
- The API container logs `libgssapi_krb5.so.2: cannot open shared object file` once at startup.
  Npgsql looks for Kerberos, which the slim runtime image doesn't include. It's harmless here
  (password auth). I didn't change the Dockerfile.
- The first startup logs a "Failed executing DbCommand" for `__EFMigrationsHistory`. That's EF's
  normal check before the table exists.
- The walkthrough left two tickets (one closed, one approved and short of stock) in the compose
  `resourcehub` database volume. `docker compose down -v` resets it.
- `HubDbContext` still uses a primary constructor (from PA1). The HealthController comment says
  Semgrep can't parse those. I left it as it was; all the new classes use classic constructors.
- `.ai_logs/conceptual_journal.md` shows as modified in git. I didn't touch it.
- Not done: real authentication, rate limiting, expiry of keys or vouchers (out of scope in spec section 8).

## Commands run / test results

- `dotnet build ../ResourceHub.slnx`: succeeded, no warnings shown.
- `dotnet restore ResourceHub.slnx --locked-mode`: succeeded, so the lock files are consistent.
- `docker compose up -d db`, then
  `RESOURCEHUB_TEST_DB=… dotnet test ../ResourceHub.slnx`: **26 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**
  (3 health, 8 asset, 8 ticket, 7 allocation/overdue). All `resourcehub_test_*` databases were
  dropped afterwards (count 0).
- `dotnet test` without `RESOURCEHUB_TEST_DB`: 2 passed, 24 skipped, 0 failed.
- `docker compose up -d --build`: the migration `InitialHub` applied on startup. Walkthrough results:
  - health 200 `{"status":"ok","database":"ok"}`
  - asset list 200 (the four seeded assets)
  - Dr. Chen's ticket POST 201 (2 laptops for 21 days, 1 JetBrains key, 750 credit)
  - IT director's pending list 200 (1 ticket)
  - approve 200
  - allocate 200: 2 `HW-…` tokens due in 21 days, key `JBIDE-7K2M-Q9XA`, 750.00 credit
  - allocations listing 200 (2 checked out, 1 key, 750 credit)
  - return 200 (laptop available units 4)
  - close 200
  - ticket detail 200: 5 events (submitted, approved, allocation_succeeded, device_returned, closed) and timings
- Over-allocation: Dr. Ferreira asked for 4 JetBrains keys (pool of 3, 2 left) plus 100 credit.
  Approve 200, then allocate **409 "Not enough stock"** with `shortages: [{JetBrains, requested 4, available 2}]`.
  Afterwards the license still had 2 keys available and the voucher balance was unchanged at
  4250.00. The ticket stayed `approved` with one `allocation_failed` event
  ("requested 4, available 2").
- Role checks: no header gave 401; an instructor calling allocate got 403.

2. **Who may do what:**
   - Instructors and advisors submit tickets only for their own course or lab.
   - The IT director approves or rejects.
   - The administrator manages assets, allocates, returns devices and closes tickets.
   - Delete: the requester or the administrator. Contents: the requester only.

   than 403, so ticket ids can't be probed. A request for another group's allocations gets 403.
   The asset catalog is open to every known user.
4. **Status flags:**
   - `reserved`: units requested on approved tickets not yet allocated.
   - `checkedout`: out and not past due.
   - `overdue`: out and past due.
   - The `availability` filter takes one flag. License and voucher assets only match `available`
     (while keys or balance remain).
5. **Changing totals with PUT:**

     refused (409) if remaining would go below zero.
